snapshots.restoreWarn3: Expect downtime until the Droplet finishes restoring and you redeploy if needed.
snapshots.restoreAck: I understand this will destroy all data on the Droplet that was created after the snapshot.

step1.title: Step 1 — Point to Project
step1.subtitle: Tell the pipeline where your Node.js project lives and which deployment profile to configure.
step1.projectPathGotcha: Mount your project directory into the container so this path is accessible.
step1.name: Name
step1.profileHint: Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only.
step1.importDesc: Browse to the .wappler/project.json inside your Wappler project. SSH host, key, and port are pre-filled — add-on services are configured separately in Step 5.
step1.importTip: 💡 The .wappler folder is hidden by default — press Ctrl+H in your file manager (or Cmd+Shift+. on macOS) to show hidden folders.
step1.importReviewHint: Wappler’s guess isn’t always right — adjust hosting target, SSH user, or key path here. Values are written to Step 4 when you click Apply.
step1.sshKeyOsHint: No Wappler project key found — point this at your usual ~/.ssh key (e.g. id_ed25519).
step1.sshKeyOsFound: Using an SSH key found in your home .ssh folder.
step1.addonsWarning: ⚠ Add-on services (Traefik, Redis, etc.) are not imported — configure them in Step 5.
step1.importApplied: ✓ Settings from this file are applied to the wizard. Change the path and click Import to refresh, or use Apply & continue again after re-importing.

projectPath.title: Project root path
projectPath.body: The absolute path to the root directory of your Node.js project — the folder that contains package.json. If running this tool in Docker, the project must be mounted as a volume.
projectPath.gotcha: Mount your project directory into the container so this path is accessible. Example: -v /home/user/my-app:/projects/my-app

profileMode.title: Deployment profile
profileMode.body: Profiles let you maintain separate configurations for different environments — e.g. staging, production, demo. Each profile has its own generated files and its own deployment target.
profileMode.gotcha: Profiles are fully independent. Changing a setting in 'staging' never affects 'production'.

step2.title: Step 2 — Build environment
step2.subtitle: How your app is built for Docker. Server CPU and host OS are configured in Step 4 once you know where you deploy.
step2.containerNote: Container image: WDP generates Dockerfile.deploy from your project's package.json (Node version, dependencies). This is separate from the Droplet host OS you choose in Step 4.
step2.subtitleExisting: Your linked Droplet already has an OS — WDP will not upgrade or reinstall it. Step 2 below applies only if you provision a new Droplet later.
step2.subtitleProvision: Choose the OS image for a new Droplet WDP will create. This does not change servers you import by IP.
step2.osExistingHint: Changing this does not modify an existing Droplet. Deploy uses whatever OS is already on the server (see banner above).

hostOs.title: Existing Droplet — OS is not changed by deploy
hostOs.body: WDP deploys your app in Docker on the server you linked in Step 4. It does not reinstall or upgrade the Droplet's operating system. The selection below is only used when you choose "Provision a new Droplet".
hostOs.mismatch: Step 2 is set to {wizard}, but this Droplet runs {host}. Deploy will use {host}. To use {wizard}, provision a new Droplet in Step 4.

rebuild.title: Change host OS (destructive rebuild)
rebuild.summary: Rebuild this Droplet from a new OS image, then run a Full deploy. Same Droplet ID and IP — everything on disk is wiped.
rebuild.dangerItem1: ALL files on this Droplet will be permanently deleted — apps, uploads, databases, Docker volumes, configs, logs, SSH-installed packages, everything.
rebuild.dangerItem2: DigitalOcean rebuild is irreversible. Take snapshots and export databases before continuing.
rebuild.dangerItem3: The Droplet keeps the same name and usually the same public IP, but the disk is a fresh install.
rebuild.dangerItem4: WDP will reinstall Docker via SSH, then run a Full deploy. Expect significant downtime.
rebuild.archLocked: CPU architecture stays {arch} (from your Droplet — cannot change on rebuild).
rebuild.step9Hint: To rebuild later: pick a new OS, then confirm on Step 9 (Deploy).
rebuild.keepCurrentOsHint: No rebuild — continue with the OS already on this Droplet.
rebuild.sameOsHint: Target OS matches the Droplet today — choose a different OS above to enable rebuild, or click Keep current OS.

targetOs.title: Target OS
targetOs.body: The OS image used when WDP provisions a new DigitalOcean Droplet. Your app still runs inside a Docker container — this is the host OS, not the Node base image in Dockerfile.deploy.
targetOs.bodyExisting: For an existing Droplet, this choice is ignored at deploy time. WDP never reimages a server you already own — it only SSHs in and runs Docker.
targetOs.gotchaProvision: Only applied when Step 4 is set to "Provision a new Droplet".
targetOs.gotchaExisting: Does not change the OS on an existing server. Check the amber banner for the Droplet's real OS.

cpuArch.title: CPU architecture
cpuArch.body: Must match the architecture of your deployment server. Most cloud providers (DigitalOcean, Hetzner, Linode) use x86_64. ARM64 is used by Raspberry Pi, Oracle's always-free ARM tier, and AWS Graviton instances.
cpuArch.gotcha: Using the wrong architecture will cause the container to fail to start on the target host.

step3.title: Step 3 — Database
step3.subtitle: Configure the database for this deployment profile.
step3.name: Database name
step3.skipDesc: Use only when the app has no database, or you manage DB credentials entirely outside WDP.
step3.intentTitle: How should this deployment connect to a database?
step3.intentManaged: WDP runs a new DB container
step3.intentManagedDesc: PostgreSQL or MySQL in the same Docker Compose stack as your app.
step3.intentExistingDesc: Cloud hosted (DO, PlanetScale) or a server you manage. WDP only writes connection settings.
step3.intentSkipDesc: No database in this app, or you will configure DB_* variables manually in Step 8.
step3.skipActiveNote: WDP will not generate a database service or DB_HOST / DB_NAME environment variables. If your Wappler app uses a database, choose "I already have a database" instead, or add credentials to .env.deploy in Step 8.
step3.managedWarningBody: WDP will create a fresh database container in this deployment stack. It will not import or connect to an existing database on your server or in Wappler dev unless you switch to External / self-hosted.
step3.managedAck: I understand WDP will create a new database container and will not migrate existing data.
step3.externalSafeNote: WDP will only store connection settings in .env.deploy. It will not create, modify, or delete data on your database server.

locDesc.managed: The pipeline manages a database container alongside your app. Simplest setup.
locDesc.external: Use a hosted database such as DigitalOcean Managed Database or PlanetScale.
locDesc.selfhosted: Connect to a database server you already manage on your own infrastructure.

step3.connDetailsNote: used inside the Docker Compose network

sslModeDesc.require: Encrypt the connection but do not verify the server certificate.
sslModeDesc.verify-ca: Verify the server certificate was signed by a trusted CA.
sslModeDesc.verify-full: Verify the CA and that the server hostname matches the certificate.

step3.sqliteNote: SQLite uses a local file — no connection details are needed. This is only suitable for local development and testing, not for production deployments.

skipDb.title: Skip database configuration
skipDb.body: Enable when your app does not use a database, or when you manage the database connection entirely outside WDP (for example cloud DB credentials you add manually in Step 8). If you have an existing database, use External or self-hosted instead of skip.
skipDb.gotcha: Skipping database while your Wappler app expects DB_* variables will cause runtime errors on data routes.

dbType.title: Database type
dbType.body: Choose the database engine your Wappler app connects to. PostgreSQL is the recommended choice for production. SQLite should only be used for local development — it has no concurrent write support.
dbType.gotcha: SQLite is not suitable for production. It cannot handle concurrent writes and has no network access for external connections.

dbLocation.title: Database location
dbLocation.body: 'Same stack' spins up a database container managed by this pipeline's docker-compose file. 'External' points to a hosted database you've provisioned separately. 'Self-hosted' points to an existing database server you manage.

dbHost.title: Database host
dbHost.body: The hostname or IP address of your database server.
dbHost.defaultHint: db.example.com or your managed DB hostname

dbPort.title: Database port
dbPort.body: The port your database listens on.

dbName.title: Database name
dbName.body: The name of the database your app connects to. This will be created if it does not exist when the stack starts.

dbUser.title: Database username
dbUser.body: The user your application authenticates as when connecting to the database.

dbPassword.title: Database password
dbPassword.body: The password for the database user above. Use a strong, unique value. This is stored in the profile's env block in wdp-config.json and never committed to git.
dbPassword.gotcha: The generated docker-compose.deploy.yml is automatically git-ignored to prevent secrets from leaking into your repository.

sslTls.title: Database SSL / TLS
sslTls.body: Managed databases (DigitalOcean, RDS, PlanetScale, etc.) typically require SSL. Certificate files must be accessible inside this Docker container — mount them as a Docker volume.
sslTls.gotcha: DigitalOcean Managed Databases require sslmode=require at minimum and provide a CA certificate file. Download it from the database cluster's connection details page.

sslCaPath.title: CA certificate path
sslCaPath.body: Path to the CA certificate file (.crt or .pem) inside the container. For DigitalOcean Managed Databases, download the CA cert from your cluster's connection details page.
sslCaPath.gotcha: Mount this file into the container using a Docker secret or bind mount. Never bake certificate files into the image.

sslCertPath.title: Client certificate
sslCertPath.body: Path to the client certificate file. Only required if the database server demands mutual TLS (mTLS). Leave blank for most managed databases.
sslCertPath.defaultHint: Optional — leave blank if not using mTLS

sslKeyPath.title: Client private key
sslKeyPath.body: Path to the client private key file. Required alongside the client certificate for mTLS.
sslKeyPath.defaultHint: Optional — leave blank if not using mTLS

step4.title: Step 4 — Hosting Target
step4.subtitle: Where should this profile deploy to?

targetDesc.digitalocean: Deploy to a DigitalOcean Droplet via SSH.
targetDesc.railway: Deploy to Railway via the Railway API.
targetDesc.vps: Any server reachable via SSH — Hetzner, Linode, OVH, your own hardware.
targetDesc.local: Deploy to the local Docker daemon. Ideal for dev and staging.

step4.existingDropletDesc: Link your Droplet or enter SSH details. WDP connects to that server as-is — it will not change the Droplet OS.
step4.provisionDropletDesc: Choose region, size, SSH key, and host OS — WDP creates a new Droplet via the DO API.

hostOs.title: Existing Droplet — host OS will not be changed
hostOs.body: Deploy syncs your project and runs Docker on this server. WDP does not upgrade Ubuntu, reinstall the OS, or reimage a Droplet you already have.

rebuild.title: Change host OS (destructive rebuild)
rebuild.summary: Rebuild this Droplet from a new OS image, then run a Full deploy. Same Droplet ID and IP — everything on disk is wiped.
rebuild.dangerItem1: ALL files on this Droplet will be permanently deleted — apps, uploads, databases, Docker volumes, configs, logs, SSH-installed packages, everything.
rebuild.dangerItem2: DigitalOcean rebuild is irreversible. Take snapshots and export databases before continuing.
rebuild.dangerItem3: The Droplet keeps the same name and usually the same public IP, but the disk is a fresh install.
rebuild.dangerItem4: WDP will reinstall Docker via SSH, then run a Full deploy. Expect significant downtime.
rebuild.archLocked: CPU architecture stays {arch} (from your Droplet — cannot change on rebuild).
rebuild.step9Hint: To rebuild later: pick a new OS, then confirm on Step 9 (Deploy).
rebuild.keepCurrentOsHint: No rebuild — continue with the OS already on this Droplet.
rebuild.sameOsHint: Target OS matches the Droplet today — choose a different OS above to enable rebuild, or click Keep current OS.

step4.newDropletDesc: WDP will create the Droplet via the DO API when you deploy. The server IP is not known yet — SSH connection details will be populated automatically once the Droplet is provisioned.
step4.doApiTokenOptional: Optional if you already saved a token in Settings → DigitalOcean.
step4.usingGlobalDoKey: ✓ Using the API token from Settings — you can leave this blank unless you need a different account.
step4.sshKeyValidatePlaceholder: Validate API token above to load keys automatically
step4.sshKeysLoading: Loading SSH keys from your DigitalOcean account…
step4.sshKeysLoadHint: Your Settings API token can load keys without re-entering it.
step4.noSshKeys: No SSH keys found on this account. Add one at cloud.digitalocean.com/account/security.
step4.importDropletDesc: Pick a Droplet from your account — WDP fills SSH host, Droplet ID, region, and size.
step4.importDropletOk: Droplet linked — SSH details updated below.
step4.importDropletLoadFail: Could not load Droplets from DigitalOcean.
step4.importDropletEmpty: No Droplets found in this account.
step4.importDropletNudgeBody: Droplet selected — choose your Wappler project root in Step 1 to continue the wizard.
step4.railwayNote: Railway deployment configuration will be collected here in a future phase when the deployment engine is built. For now, selecting Railway records your intent.
step4.localDockerNote: Local Docker deployment runs on this machine's Docker (same as Wappler). No SSH details are needed — the pipeline will run docker compose up -d directly.

sshDetails.title: SSH connection details
sshDetails.body: These are used to connect to your server for deployment. Key-based authentication only — password auth is never used. These details are also used by the SSH Terminal tab on the profile dashboard.
sshDetails.gotcha: The private key must be readable by this Docker container. Mount the .ssh directory as a volume if it lives on your host machine.

sshHost.title: SSH host
sshHost.body: The IP address or hostname of your server.

sshUser.title: SSH user
sshUser.body: The user to authenticate as on the remote server.

sshKey.title: SSH private key path
sshKey.body: Absolute path to the private key file on disk, as seen from inside this Docker container. Only key-based auth is supported — password SSH is never used.
sshKey.gotcha: Mount your ~/.ssh directory into the container: -v ~/.ssh:/root/.ssh:ro

remotePath.title: Remote deploy path
remotePath.body: Absolute path on the server where project files will be uploaded. Leave blank to use the default: /opt/app-name

newDroplet.title: Provision new Droplet
newDroplet.body: WDP will call the DigitalOcean API to create a Droplet with these settings on first deploy.

doApiToken.title: DO API token
doApiToken.body: Your DigitalOcean personal access token with write scope. Used to create the Droplet via the DO API. Stored only in your local profile config.
doApiToken.gotcha: Keep this token secret — it has full account access. You can create a scoped token at cloud.digitalocean.com/account/api/tokens

doRegion.title: Droplet region
doRegion.body: The DigitalOcean datacenter region to deploy to. Choose the region closest to your users.

doSize.title: Droplet size
doSize.body: The CPU and RAM allocated to the Droplet. For most Wappler apps with a database, 2 GB RAM is the practical minimum in production.
doSize.gotcha: 1 GB RAM is often too small once Node.js, the database, and add-on services are all running.

doSshKey.title: SSH key
doSshKey.body: The SSH key to install on the new Droplet. Select from the keys registered in your DigitalOcean account. Validate your API token above to load the list.
doSshKey.defaultHint: Validate your API token first to load your keys

step5.title: Step 5 — Add-ons
step5.subtitle: Select optional services to include in the generated deployment stack. All add-ons are opt-in.
step5.requiredNote: Required fields are marked * and must be filled before you can proceed.
step5.localWarningTitle: Local Docker deployment — some add-ons have limitations
step5.localWarningDesc: Let's Encrypt / ACME requires a public domain and will not work locally. If Traefik is enabled, it will be configured for HTTP-only routing. Add-ons that rely on public URLs (Plausible, n8n webhooks) will run but external access will not be available.

addonDesc.traefik: Reverse proxy + automatic Let's Encrypt SSL
addonDesc.minio: S3-compatible self-hosted object storage for uploads
addonDesc.plausible: Self-hosted Community Edition (AGPL) — not paid Plausible Cloud
addonDesc.apprise: Deploy notifications to Discord, Slack, Telegram, etc.

step5.traefikLocalNote: Let's Encrypt (ACME) is not available for local deployments. Traefik will be configured as an HTTP-only reverse proxy with no TLS cert resolver.
step5.traefikModeBundledHint: WDP runs Traefik on ports 80/443 for this project (dedicated server or single app).
step5.traefikModeExternalHint: Shared staging — join your server’s Traefik network; WDP will not start another proxy.
step5.traefikExternalNote: Your server already handles HTTPS on ports 80/443. Enter the Docker network your Traefik uses (must match the running instance). Cert resolver name must match that Traefik’s config. WDP will not stop other sites during deploy.
step5.redisWapplerNote: Wappler Project Target / Server Connect Redis settings are for local development. For production, choose how this deployment connects to Redis below. WDP writes REDIS_URL into .env.deploy for your app container.
step5.redisModeManagedHint: New redis:7-alpine container on the internal Docker network (hostname redis).
step5.redisModeExisting: Use existing Redis on this server
step5.redisModeExistingHint: Connect to a Redis container you already run (e.g. from a Wappler deploy). No new Redis container in this stack.
step5.redisModeExternalHint: Cloud Redis (Upstash, DigitalOcean, etc.). Connection string only.
step5.redisManagedWarning: WDP will deploy a separate Redis container in this stack. Session or cache data in an existing Redis elsewhere will not be migrated automatically.
step5.redisManagedAck: I understand WDP will create a new Redis container for this deployment.
step5.redisScanNone: No Redis containers detected on this host.
step5.dnsRegistrarTitle: New or existing domain? Set up DNS at your registrar
step5.dnsRegistrarBody:
WDP cannot change settings at your domain registrar (e.g. Fasthosts, GoDaddy, Namecheap). You must point the domain at your server before https:// and Let's Encrypt will work.

  • Option A — keep registrar DNS: In your domain control panel, add an A record: host @ → your Droplet IP. Add www → same IP, or a CNAME www → your domain.
  • Option B — use DigitalOcean DNS: At your registrar, set nameservers to DigitalOcean’s. Then create A/CNAME records in the DigitalOcean control panel (or use Server → DNS on this profile after deploy).

Changes can take from a few minutes up to 48 hours to propagate. The domain field above is only the name Traefik uses — it does not configure your registrar for you.
step5.traefikIncludeWww: Also secure www (apex + www in one certificate)

domain.title: Domain
domain.body: The public domain name Traefik will route to your app (usually the apex, e.g. example.com). With “Also secure www” enabled, HTTPS and the certificate cover both apex and www.
domain.gotcha: Let's Encrypt will fail if DNS for each hostname does not resolve to this server before you deploy.

traefikIncludeWww.title: Apex + www TLS
traefikIncludeWww.body: Adds www.your-domain to the same Traefik routers and Let's Encrypt certificate as the domain above. Requires a DNS A or CNAME record for www pointing at this server.
traefikIncludeWww.gotcha: Turn off only if you do not use www or www points elsewhere.

acmeEmail.title: ACME email
acmeEmail.body: Email address for Let's Encrypt certificate registration and expiry notices. Must be a real, monitored address.

traefikNetwork.title: Traefik Docker network
traefikNetwork.body: The Docker network Traefik attaches to when WDP deploys its own Traefik (default traefik-public).

traefikNetworkExternal.title: Existing Traefik network
traefikNetworkExternal.body: The external Docker network your server’s Traefik already uses. The app container joins this network so Traefik can route your domain to it. Common values: traefik-public, wappler-compose_proxy.
traefikNetworkExternal.gotcha: Must exist on the server before deploy (WDP can create it if missing, but Traefik must already be attached to it).

certResolver.title: Cert resolver
certResolver.body: The name of the ACME resolver referenced in Traefik labels and the Traefik static config.

traefikDashboard.title: Traefik dashboard
traefikDashboard.body: Enables the Traefik web UI. Should never be exposed publicly without authentication.
traefikDashboard.gotcha: Do not expose the Traefik dashboard on a public port without putting it behind authentication.

redisPassword.title: Redis password
redisPassword.body: For managed Redis, this sets requirepass on the new container and REDIS_PASSWORD in .env.deploy. For existing/external Redis, enter the password your instance expects (leave blank if none).
redisPassword.gotcha: A passwordless Redis instance is a serious security risk on any network-accessible server.

redisHost.title: Redis host
redisHost.body: Hostname the app container uses to reach Redis. For an existing Docker Redis on the same host, use the container name and join its Docker network below.
redisHost.gotcha: localhost inside the app container is not your server's Redis — use the Docker service/container name or an external hostname.

redisNetwork.title: Docker network
redisNetwork.body: If existing Redis runs in another compose project, enter that project's Docker network so the app container can reach Redis. Leave blank if Redis is on the public hostname or you use external managed Redis.
redisNetwork.gotcha: The network must already exist on the server before deploy.

redisPort.title: Redis port
redisPort.body: TCP port your Redis instance listens on.

redisDbIndex.title: Redis database index
redisDbIndex.body: Redis logical database number (0–15). Written into REDIS_URL as /db.

redisMaxmemory.title: Redis maxmemory
redisMaxmemory.body: Optional memory cap, e.g. 256mb. Prevents Redis from consuming all available RAM.

redisEviction.title: Redis eviction policy
redisEviction.body: What Redis does when maxmemory is reached. allkeys-lru removes the least-recently-used key.

minioUser.title: MinIO root user
minioUser.body: The admin username / S3 access key for MinIO.

minioPassword.title: MinIO root password
minioPassword.body: Admin password / S3 secret key. Minimum 8 characters.
minioPassword.gotcha: Use a strong password. This is the master credential for your object storage.

minioBucket.title: Default bucket
minioBucket.body: A bucket to create on first start. Useful for your app's uploads directory.

portainerUiPort.title: Portainer UI port
portainerUiPort.body: Port Portainer's web UI will be accessible on.

uptimeKumaPort.title: Uptime Kuma port
uptimeKumaPort.body: Port the Uptime Kuma web UI will be accessible on.

plausibleDomain.title: Plausible domain
plausibleDomain.body: The hostname your self-hosted Plausible CE instance is served from (Traefik or port). Not the same as signing up at plausible.io — WDP deploys the free Community Edition image on your server.

plausiblePort.title: Plausible port
plausiblePort.body: Host port for the Plausible web UI.

plausibleSecretKey.title: Plausible secret key base
plausibleSecretKey.body: 64-character hex string used for session encryption. Leave blank to auto-generate.

mailpitSmtpPort.title: Mailpit SMTP port
mailpitSmtpPort.body: Port Mailpit listens on for incoming SMTP messages from your app.

mailpitUiPort.title: Mailpit UI port
mailpitUiPort.body: Port for the Mailpit web inbox UI.

n8nPort.title: n8n port
n8nPort.body: Host port for the n8n web UI.

n8nEncryptionKey.title: n8n encryption key
n8nEncryptionKey.body: Used to encrypt saved credentials in n8n. Auto-generated 32-char hex if blank. Must remain consistent across restarts — it is stored in wdp-config.json.

n8nWebhookUrl.title: n8n webhook URL
n8nWebhookUrl.body: External URL n8n is reachable at — needed for webhook triggers to work. Only required if n8n is exposed via Traefik.

resticRepo.title: Restic repository
resticRepo.body: Where backups are stored. Can be a local path, an S3 URL (s3:https://…), a MinIO endpoint, or Backblaze B2.

resticPassword.title: Restic repository password
resticPassword.body: Encryption password for the Restic repository. Keep this safe — without it you cannot restore your backups.
resticPassword.gotcha: Losing this password means losing access to all backups. Store it securely outside the server.

appriseNotifyUrl.title: Apprise notification URL
appriseNotifyUrl.body: An Apprise-format URL or a plain HTTPS webhook. Examples: discord://webhookid/token, slack://tokenA/tokenB/tokenC, tgram://bottoken/chatid

step6.title: Step 6 — Resources & Scaling
step6.subtitle: Configure how many instances of your app run and what resource limits each container has.
step6.horizontalDesc: Run multiple replicas of your app container in parallel.
step6.redisRequired: Redis add-on becomes required when scaling horizontally — session storage must be shared across all replicas.
step6.minioRecommended: MinIO is strongly recommended over a local bind mount for the uploads/ volume to avoid split-brain file access across replicas.
step6.healthcheckDesc: Docker automatically restarts your app container if it becomes unhealthy. Requires a /health endpoint in your app.

horizontal.title: Horizontal scaling
horizontal.body: Runs multiple identical replicas of your app container. Requires Redis for shared session storage, and MinIO is strongly recommended over a local bind mount for uploaded files to avoid split-brain access.
horizontal.gotcha: All replicas must share the same SESSION_SECRET value. Redis add-on becomes required — session data must be stored centrally, not in individual container memory.

replicaCount.title: Replica count
replicaCount.body: How many instances of your app container to run simultaneously. Load is distributed between them.

memLimit.title: Memory limit
memLimit.body: Sets the mem_limit in the generated Compose file. Prevents a runaway container from consuming all available RAM and OOM-killing other services on the host.
memLimit.defaultHint: Leave blank for no limit — e.g. 512m, 1g
memLimit.gotcha: Critical on small droplets (1–2 GB RAM). Without a limit, a memory leak in your app can take down the entire server.

cpuLimit.title: CPU limit
cpuLimit.body: Sets the cpus limit in the generated Compose file. Useful on multi-tenant hosts where you want to prevent one service from monopolising all CPU cores.
cpuLimit.defaultHint: Leave blank for no limit — e.g. 0.5 (half a core), 1.0 (one core)

healthcheck.title: Docker HEALTHCHECK
healthcheck.body: Configures a HEALTHCHECK instruction in the generated Dockerfile.deploy. Docker will periodically send an HTTP request to your app's health endpoint. If it fails repeatedly, Docker automatically restarts the container.
healthcheck.gotcha: Without a HEALTHCHECK, Docker has no way to detect that your app has crashed or locked up. It will continue routing traffic to a dead container.

step7.title: Step 7 — Security Scanning
step7.subtitle: Select which security scanners run as part of the pre-deploy pipeline.
step7.blockOnCriticalDesc: The pipeline halts and deployment is refused if any scanner reports a CRITICAL severity finding.
step7.scanOnDeployDesc: When off, deploy skips npm audit and optional scanners (faster). Block-on-critical only applies when scans run.

scannerDesc.npmAudit: Checks your Node.js dependencies against the npm advisory database.
scannerDesc.osvScanner: Google's open-source vulnerability scanner. Checks dependencies against the OSV database.
scannerDesc.socketCli: Detects supply-chain attacks, malicious packages, and suspicious package changes.
scannerDesc.gitleaks: Scans git history and staged files for hardcoded secrets, API keys, and passwords.
scannerDesc.trivy: Scans the built Docker image for OS-level and language-level CVEs.
scannerDesc.grype: Generates an SBOM with Syft then scans it for vulnerabilities with Grype.
scannerDesc.dockerScout: Docker's native image vulnerability scanner. Requires Docker Hub login.

npmAudit.title: npm audit
npmAudit.body: Runs npm audit --audit-level=moderate against your project's node_modules. Always included and always enabled — cannot be disabled.

osvScanner.title: OSV-Scanner
osvScanner.body: Scans package-lock.json against the Open Source Vulnerabilities (OSV) database maintained by Google. Catches vulnerabilities not always present in the npm advisory DB.

socketCli.title: Socket CLI
socketCli.body: Socket.dev's CLI checks your dependencies for known supply-chain threats, typosquatting, and suspicious author/maintainer changes — catches things CVE databases miss.
socketCli.defaultHint: Recommended — especially for supply chain attack prevention

gitleaks.title: Gitleaks
gitleaks.body: Detects hardcoded credentials, tokens, and API keys committed to the repository — including in git history.
gitleaks.gotcha: Gitleaks will fail the pipeline if it finds secrets. Fix them with git-filter-repo before deploying — do not just add them to .gitleaksignore without reviewing each finding.

trivy.title: Trivy
trivy.body: Aqua Security's Trivy scans the final Docker image layers for CVEs in both OS packages (Alpine, Debian) and application dependencies.

grype.title: Grype + Syft
grype.body: Syft generates a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for the Docker image. Grype then scans that SBOM for known vulnerabilities. The SBOM is saved as a build artefact.
grype.defaultHint: Recommended — SBOM is a useful compliance artefact

dockerScout.title: Docker Scout
dockerScout.body: Docker Scout analyses the image and compares it against Docker's own vulnerability database. Useful if you push to Docker Hub. Requires a Docker Hub account and CLI login.
dockerScout.gotcha: Requires docker login inside the pipeline runner. Configure Docker Hub credentials as environment variables before enabling.

blockOnCritical.title: Block on critical
blockOnCritical.body: When enabled, the pipeline will halt and refuse to deploy if any enabled scanner reports a critical-severity finding. Findings at other severity levels are reported but do not block deployment.
blockOnCritical.gotcha: Enabling this is strongly recommended for production environments. For development pipelines you may want to leave it off to avoid being blocked by unfixed upstream CVEs.

step8.title: Step 8 — Generate Files
step8.subtitle: Review your configuration, then generate your deployment files.
step8.envWarning: Keep .env.deploy secret. Replace all CHANGE_ME placeholders before deploying.
step8.notGeneratedHint: Click "Generate files" to produce your deployment configuration.
step8.notGeneratedProfile: Not yet generated for this profile.
step8.fileNotFound: File not found in generation output.
step8.envNotice: .env.deploy contains secrets and is gitignored automatically. Never commit this file. Replace all CHANGE_ME placeholders before deploying.
step8.emptyStateBody: Click Generate files to produce your deployment files from your wizard configuration.

step9.title: Step 9 — Deploy
step9.subtitle: Run a pre-deploy readiness check, then deploy to your target.
step9.noProfile: ⚠ No active profile selected. Go back to Step 1 and select or create a profile.

deploy.publishAvailableHint: Routine code updates: Publish syncs your project and rebuilds the app image using Docker/npm cache (no full re-download when package-lock.json is unchanged). No security scans. Use Full deploy after wizard or infra changes.
deploy.publishAfterFirstDeploy: Complete a successful Full deploy first — then Publish changes will appear for routine updates.
deploy.publishRunsChecks: Publish runs quick checks automatically when you click it.
deploy.publishNextHint: Next time, use Publish changes for routine code updates.
deploy.checksHint: Click "Run checks" to verify your deployment environment is ready.
deploy.checksWarning: ⚠ One or more checks failed. You can still deploy but results may be unreliable.
deploy.scanTimingNote: Scans run before sync/build in the deployment log above. npm audit HIGH/MEDIUM warnings do not block deploy unless you enabled “Block on critical” in Step 7.
deploy.domainPortHint: Traefik is off — browsers use port {port} for HTTP. Open http://{domain}:{port}/ (not https://{domain}). Re-enable Traefik in Step 5 for standard HTTPS on port 443.

rebuild.title: Danger zone — Rebuild Droplet OS
rebuild.summary: Wipe this Droplet and reinstall from a new OS image, then Full deploy your app. Use only when you need a new host OS on the same Droplet.
rebuild.dangerHeading: You will lose ALL data on this Droplet
rebuild.dangerItem1: Every file on the server is permanently destroyed — application data, database files, Docker images/volumes, Traefik certs, manual configs, cron jobs, all of it.
rebuild.dangerItem2: Create a DigitalOcean snapshot and back up databases before proceeding. This cannot be undone.
rebuild.dangerItem3: The Droplet ID and public IP are usually unchanged, but the disk is completely empty after rebuild.
rebuild.dangerItem4: Downtime is expected while the OS reinstalls, Docker is installed, and WDP runs a Full deploy.
rebuild.archLocked: Architecture: {arch} (fixed — must match your Droplet size).
rebuild.acknowledge: I understand that ALL data on this Droplet will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered without my own backups.
rebuild.confirmLabel: Type the Droplet name "{name}" to confirm:
rebuild.confirmMismatch: Name does not match — type it exactly as shown on DigitalOcean.
rebuild.checksNote: Take a snapshot first (profile → Server → Snapshots). Ensure Step 8 files are generated and your DO SSH key is in Step 4.
rebuild.keepCurrentOsHint: No rebuild — continue with the OS already on this Droplet.
rebuild.sameOsHint: Selected OS matches your Droplet — pick a different OS to enable rebuild, or cancel to continue without changes.

deploy.scanBlockedHint: Dismiss findings below to allow deployment, or fix them before re-deploying.
deploy.backupBeforeFix: Backup package.json & package-lock.json before applying fixes
deploy.forceWarning: --force upgrades to the latest major versions and may introduce breaking changes. Review your app after running it.
deploy.checksFirstHint: Run checks first to enable the deploy button.
deploy.scanBlockingDeploy: ⛔ Blocked by undismissed critical finding(s) — see Security scan results above.
deploy.checksWarningDeploy: Checks have warnings — deploy at your own risk.
deploy.healthHint: Confirms the app is responding and accepting HTTP requests.
deploy.cleanupHint: Remove unused Docker resources on the target host to free up disk space. Only runs after a passing health check.

git.sharedPathWarning: This folder is also used by profile(s): {profiles}. Git and generate actions affect the same directory — set a unique project path in Step 1 for each profile.
git.initBody: Creates a git repository in your Wappler project folder, adds WDP-safe .gitignore rules (secrets stay local), and optionally commits generated wdp/ files. Nothing is sent to GitHub until you add a remote and push.
git.initFirstCommit: Create first commit for wdp/ files (if any exist)
git.initSuccess: Git is ready for this project.
git.initAlreadyRepo: Project was already a git repository — .gitignore refreshed
git.initRemoteHint: Further commits, diffs, and GitHub push will come in a later WDP release. For now use git on the server or your IDE if you need more.
git.repoActiveBody: This project already has git. WDP Phase A only covers initial setup (.gitignore and optional first commit). Use your terminal or IDE for day-to-day git until WDP adds GitHub integration.
git.comingSoonNote: Coming later in WDP: diff and commit wdp/ files, deploy tags, GitHub token in Settings, and push from the app.
git.noDiffChanges: No tracked files have changed since the last commit.
git.tagDesc: Tags HEAD and pushes to origin.

knowledge.title: Project Knowledge
knowledge.subtitle: Generate a knowledge base from your project source files for use with the AI assistant.
knowledge.notGeneratedHint: Click "Generate knowledge" to analyse your project.

ai.title: AI Assistant

ai.inputHint: Shift+Enter for new line · Enter to send

settings.title: Settings
settings.openrouterKeyHint: Get a key at openrouter.ai — it is stored on the server and never sent to the browser.
settings.doSectionDesc: Default API token for all DigitalOcean profiles. Used when provisioning Droplets, managing DNS, and the Server tab — unless a profile has its own token.
settings.doApiKeyHint: Create a personal access token at
settings.clearDoKeyConfirm: Clear the stored DigitalOcean API token?
settings.csSectionDesc: Send SMS alerts on deploy success, failure, and rollback. Uses the mobile number from My Profile (include your dialling code).
settings.csApiKeyHint: Write-only after save — get credentials from your ClickSend dashboard.
settings.csTestHint: Sends a test message to your My Profile mobile number in your current UI language.

staleGenerate.title: Regenerate deployment files
staleGenerate.bodyChanged: Your wizard settings have changed since Docker files were last generated (Step 8). Regenerate Dockerfile.deploy, docker-compose.deploy.yml, and .env.deploy before deploying so the server matches your profile.
staleGenerate.bodyNever: You have not generated deployment files yet. Complete Step 8 to create Dockerfile.deploy, docker-compose.deploy.yml, and .env.deploy before your first deploy.
staleGenerate.bodyMissing: Generated deployment files are missing from your project folder. Open Step 8 and regenerate them before deploying.

dirBrowser.heading: Browse to project root
dirBrowser.hiddenFoldersHint: Hidden folders (e.g. .wappler) are shown so you can open project.json.

remoteDocker.subtitleOptional: Optional check — skip if Docker is already set up or you will install it yourself.

remoteDocker.deployCheckHint: Fix the server (Server tab → Install Docker, or the troubleshooting doc) then re-run checks.

about.purpose: WDP is a self-hosted deployment pipeline built specifically for Wappler projects using Docker. It walks you through configuring your stack, generates production-ready Dockerfiles and Compose files, runs security scans, and deploys directly to your server, all from one clean interface.
about.tagline: Created for the Wappler Community — shared with ❤️ for Docker users.
